recipe: Native check as the method defines it (PCRL in-sample one-hot ridge R2 1e-6; dg certificate = same on all cell rows; dominant-axis variant reported separately)
fitted_defense_parameters_or_basis: yes (it is the method's own check)
fitting_rows: assessment (same rows as scoring; historical: test split or all dg cell rows)
notes: Reported verbatim as the method's own test; never pooled with attacker rows. float64 recomputation reported beside the historical float32 value.

recipe: Held-out multinomial logistic regression on the release (StandardScaler fit on attacker_fit; L2)
notes: In-scope linear-family test for LEACE/SPLINCE/erase layer (convex log-loss) and for INLP's own stopping rule; metric AUC (macro OvR + supported worst-class/pair) and held-out log-loss reduction over prior.

recipe: Held-out linear OLS-R2 on the release: affine one-hot regression fit on attacker_fit with means from attacker_fit; scored on assessment with attacker_fit intercepts; numerical floor = drop covariance directions with eigenvalue < 1e-6 x largest; ridge penalty relative (lambda = rho * trace(S)/d)
notes: THE within-scope test for the native R2 check (C2 if native passes and this exceeds tau with UCB/LCB rule). Also report unfloored OLS and the historical fixed-penalty ridge separately (scale dependence; SCOPE_CORRECTIONS D1, A4). Same tau grid as the native check.

recipe: Gradient-boosted trees on the release (sklearn HistGradientBoostingClassifier)
selection_rows: attacker_val (log-loss; early stopping on a split of attacker_fit only)
budget: 20 random configs: learning_rate {0.03,0.1,0.3}; max_leaf_nodes {15,31,63}; min_samples_leaf {20,50,100}; l2 {0,1}; max_iter 500 with early stopping
notes: Defense-agnostic nonlinear recipient (dg Tier-1 analogue; XGB replaced by sklearn HGB for a pinned dependency-free build; fidelity check vs stored XGB on one cell).

recipe: MLP on the release (2 hidden layers; standardized inputs)
selection_rows: attacker_val (log-loss; early stopping on a split of attacker_fit only)
budget: 18 configs (full grid): hidden {64,128,256}x2; alpha {1e-5,1e-4,1e-3}; lr {1e-3,3e-3}; 3 attacker seeds per selected config (refit variance reported)

recipe: Label-only reference: predict s from the TRUE task label y of the same rows (multinomial LR on one-hot y; empirical conditional frequency table as a check)
notes: Empirical difference reference for the output surface (not an MI bound or floor). Reported with the same metrics; output leakage = output recipe minus this reference, paired over assessment units.

recipe: Output-only attacker (linear): multinomial LR on the released task output object (declared per cell: hard label | calibrated score | logit vector)
notes: Requires a frozen task head (U1). For post-hoc methods without a deployed head, the output is that of the common utility probe and is labelled as such.

recipe: Output-only attacker (nonlinear): GBT on the released task output object
budget: as R03 (10 configs; output dim is small)
notes: Compared to R05 and to R08 (clean-output reference).
Only where the release contract permits both surfaces to the same recipient; nested slate must include R01 and R06L.
Nested slate must include R03/R04 and R06N; reported increment vs best nested member.

recipe: Clean-output reference: R06N applied to the UNTREATED model's output object on the same rows
notes: Reference: what the same output object leaks without the defense.

recipe: Noise-specific Gaussian LRT with population clean vectors (stored dg 'Tier 2'; = A4 white-box population): class-conditional Gaussians fit on CLEAN pre-noise representations of the labelled attacker population; known noise covariance (and Q) added; scores ONE release
paired_clean_and_released_examples: yes (clean population vectors; not paired with releases)
notes: Distinct from R10 and R11. Never sees the target's clean vector or noise realisation; not repeated-query; not an insider. Noise channels only (for deterministic defenses it reduces to QDA on the release = R01/R03 access).

recipe: Release-only Gaussian LRT with known Sigma (A2): class-conditional Gaussians fit on NOISED releases of the attacker population with the known noise covariance subtracted from the fitted covariance
notes: Tests whether the stored R09 result depends on clean population vectors.

recipe: GENERAL adaptive (defense-aware) attacker: the attacker holds a separate labelled population with raw inputs; runs the frozen encoder and the frozen FITTED defense (published parameters: LEACE map; projection Q; sigma; C; tree cells) on it to simulate releases (stochastic channels: K=8 fresh draws per row as augmentation); trains MLP and GBT on simulated (release; s) pairs; selects among MLP/GBT configs on attacker_val simulated releases only; scores the true releases of assessment rows
paired_clean_and_released_examples: yes (simulated by the attacker from its own population)
task_outputs: no (optionally yes when the contract releases outputs; then also train on simulated outputs)
budget: 38 configs total (18 MLP as R04 + 20 GBT as R03); 3 attacker seeds; K=8 draws for stochastic channels; CPU cap 1 core-hour per cell-arm
notes: Knowing the defense is not knowing the target's clean input. For deterministic defenses R11 coincides with R03/R04 trained on releases (report as such, not as extra strength). Requires the fitted defense parameters to exist (artifact inventory); otherwise C5 'not estimable without refit'.

recipe: Repeated-release averaging attacker: averages N independent releases of the SAME target before applying the R11-selected model (or R09/R10 LRT with sigma/sqrt(N))
budget: N in {1,4,16,64,256}; same model budget as R11
notes: Only where the release contract issues fresh noise per query. Persistent per-person token => N=1 by construction (row reported as not applicable). Deterministic defenses: not applicable.

recipe: Knows-basis attacker: knows the private basis Q of the subspace channel; projects each release onto the complement of span(Q) (noise-free part) and onto span(Q); trains R01/R03 on the projected releases
notes: Prices the 'private basis' assumption of isolate-then-noise (stored dg knows_q.json is the historical analogue).

recipe: Combined-view attacker for the multi-purpose scenario: R01/R03/R04 on the concatenation of releases held by a declared coalition; nested slate includes every single-view and ancestor-view predictor and the prior
budget: as R01 + R03 + R04 per view set
notes: Targets only attributes disallowed to EVERY coalition member; reports absolute recovery and combination increment (best single view minus union) with refit replicates.

recipe: Insider stress test (A5): attacker given the target's own pre-protection representation
notes: Stress test only; never used to refute a guarantee that excludes it. Listed so the access lattice is complete; gradients/internal activations are not released by any planned arm.
